title: Claude & Levent Alpöge Construct Complex Structures on the 6-Sphere (Hopf’s 1948 Problem)
whyItMatters: Resolves Heinz Hopf’s iconic 78-year-old problem by constructing a complex structure on S⁶—triggering a wave of independent arXiv proofs and infinite families by human complex geometers.
summary: On August 23, 2026, Levent Alpöge circulated a 108-page manuscript produced with Anthropic’s Claude (alpo.ge/s6.pdf) claiming an affirmative answer to Heinz Hopf’s celebrated 1948 problem: whether the six-dimensional sphere S⁶ admits an integrable complex structure. Constructing a 1-parameter family of compact complex threefolds diffeomorphic to S⁶ by completing the (3, 4, ∞) modular family of 2-tori, the Alpöge–Claude breakthrough triggered an extraordinary response from human complex geometers—with Philip Engel (arXiv:2609.38442), Jeff Viaclovsky (arXiv:2609.33785, arXiv:2610.10451), and Wenfei Liu & Sönke Rollenske (arXiv:2609.33826) rapidly digesting, simplifying, and generalizing the construction into two-parameter and infinitely many biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures on S⁶.
technicalHighlights: Answers Heinz Hopf’s 1948 question in the affirmative by building a 1-parameter family of compact complex threefolds diffeomorphic to the standard 6-sphere S⁶.
Completes the (3, 4, ∞) modular family of 2-tori at its three special points via logarithmic transformations.

Rapidly corroborated and generalized by multiple independent human complex geometers (Engel, Viaclovsky, Liu–Rollenske) into multi-parameter and infinite families of inequivalent complex structures on S⁶.
caveats: Originally circulated as a self-hosted 108-page PDF without a Lean formalization; while multiple independent specialist arXiv preprints build directly on and extend the Alpöge–Claude construction, formal journal peer review of the original manuscript and its extensions is still completing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settles one of the most famous, longest-standing open problems in differential and complex geometry (Hopf 1948, 78 years open)—a problem that had tripped up decades of top geometers.
scoreRationale.ripple: Immediately launched a vibrant subfield of new arXiv papers constructing two-parameter families, arbitrary Kuranishi dimensions, and non-Gauduchon Hodge theory on complex S⁶.
scoreRationale.verification: No Lean formalization or completed journal refereeing yet, but unusually high independent confidence given multiple specialist arXiv papers confirming and extending the construction.
scoreRationale.velocity: Cracked a 78-year-old geometry monument in an AI-assisted breakthrough that human geometers immediately ran with.
